prerequisites: Basic knowledge of mathematics and computer science is recommended.

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge of the fundamentals of automation and control methods

Acquire a solid foundation of automatic control knowledge to enable students to analyze low and medium-level control systems, recognizing their fundamental modules and the techniques used for their design.
Adapt to the evolution of these technologies, as they have great future prospects.
Show students industrial tasks where computers, programmable logic controllers, and robots can be used as basic automation tools, raising awareness of the need for industrial sector automation.
Approach basic industrial engineering knowledge from a process automation perspective.
Offer a vision of currently automated systems in the industrial sector, allowing the application of learned concepts and techniques to real-world, market-existing systems.
Compare different systems to study their advantages and disadvantages, thereby selecting the appropriate system based on environmental characteristics.
Introduce a series of basic engineering tools for mathematical calculations, simulation, and programming, essential in process automation.

syllabus_topics: Module 1. Modeling and control of sequential processes
Topic 1. Analysis and modeling of dynamic sequential systems
Practice 1. Modeling and control of industrial sequential dynamic systems
Module 2. Modeling and control of continuous processes
Topic 4. Analysis and modeling of continuous dynamic systems
Topic 5. Design of continuous system controllers
Practice 0. Data analysis and visualization with Matlab
Practice 2. Modeling of continuous dynamic systems
Practice 3. Control of continuous dynamic systems
Practice 4. Operation of a robotic system: positioning, programming, and work
assessment_rules: The final grade is calculated as 0.3 * Practices + 0.5 * Exam + 0.2 * Continuous assessment and participation. A minimum score of 5 out of 10 is required for each activity: each of the four practices, each of the two parts of the exam, and the continuous assessment tests. For the practical part, at least 80% attendance to laboratory sessions is mandatory, otherwise, this part will be graded as 'Not apt'. Partial exam grades above 7 points may be retained for the extraordinary call; otherwise, they are not carried over. For the extraordinary call, students who did not pass practices may resubmit them, while those who did not attend will take a practical exam.
